neighbours.label: the change-of-state verb 'become/becomes/became' (X has become harder)
fire: Over the last decade, the village has become a popular weekend escape.
Since the new manager arrived, meetings have become much shorter.
By late autumn the days become noticeably colder.
Her handwriting became harder to read as she aged.
After the storm, the road becomes impassable for days.
The once-quiet street is becoming crowded with tourists.
Over time the old bridge became a symbol of the city.
With practice, the exercise becomes much easier.
quiet: Over the last decade, the village has stayed a popular weekend escape.
Since the new manager arrived, meetings have been much shorter.
By late autumn the days are noticeably colder.
Her handwriting was hard to read even when she was young.
After the storm, the road is closed for days.
The once-quiet street is crowded with tourists.
For years the old bridge was a symbol of the city.
With practice, the exercise is much easier.
